# Tool Input Validation

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
| Status | In Progress          |

Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.

## Validation at execute time

- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16), [validated by: registers a tool requiring a location string, calls execute with {}, and asserts the returned result names location as required and the executors call count is 0](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).
- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46), [validated by: asserts a wrong-typed field is rejected with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does not contain the offending value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L54), [validated by: asserts a rejected payload containing an identifying field produces no log line containing that fields value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L148)).
- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the executor unchanged](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L29)).
- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake ([validated by: execute still throws Unknown tool: <name> for an unregistered name](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L143)).

## Schema compilation and caching

- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: asserts register throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and that the thrown message names the tool](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L79)).
- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: asserts a static tool schema is compiled once across ten execute calls](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L120)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between calls is validated against the schema current at that call](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L90)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery

- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).

parameters.content:
# Tool Input Validation

| Field  | Value                |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
| Status | Implemented          |

Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.

## Validation at execute time

- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16), [validated by: registers a tool requiring a location string, calls execute with {}, and asserts the returned result names location as required and the executors call count is 0](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).
- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46), [validated by: asserts a wrong-typed field is rejected with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does not contain the offending value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L53), [validated by: asserts a rejected payload containing an identifying field produces no log line containing that fields value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L143)).
- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the executor unchanged](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L30)).
- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake ([validated by: execute still throws Unknown tool: <name> for an unregistered name](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L138)).

## Schema compilation and caching

- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: asserts register throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and that the thrown message names the tool](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L76)).
- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: asserts a static tool schema is compiled once across ten execute calls](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L117)).
- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between calls is validated against the schema current at that call](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L87)).

## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery

- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112), [validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L523)).
